svg.text: RS256 JWT verified once at Kong, scopes enforced at the gateway, mesh-internal gRPC trusted inside the VPC
Flow A - Browser login: email + password to JWT cookie + refresh token
bcrypt verify, then sign RS256 JWT (15m; sub, email, jti,
Flow B - Refresh rotation: access token expired, refresh token still valid
GET refresh:<jti>, validate family, DEL old jti
issue new JWT + new refresh token (rotated jti, same family)
Reuse of a revoked refresh token revokes the
Flow C - Agent onboarding: OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE (RFC 7636)
forward (JWT cookie validated, user must be
render scope card, user clicks Allow
store tokens in the OS keychain (never on disk)
Flow D - MCP tool call: Bearer JWT, scope enforced at the gateway
THEN call the API with a valid token
jwt plugin: verify RS256 via JWKS (kid match), check exp / iss
Flow E - Internal gRPC: no JWT, mesh-internal trust boundary
Inside the VPC + EKS NetworkPolicy. Security
groups restrict pod-to-pod traffic. No Internet
Flow F - Stripe webhook: signed payload, the signature header replaces the JWT
route bypasses the jwt plugin (allowlist), forward
verify HMAC, idempotency on stripe_event_id, UPSERT

Access JWT 15 minutes. Refresh token 7 days for browsers, 24 hours for MCP. RS256 keypair rotated quarterly, public keys served at /.well-known/jwks.json. Every 4xx/5xx auth failure is audited to CloudWatch and brute-force attempts are throttled per IP + user.
